items.title: Cal Collins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 11, 1997
items.q: I think Buddy Rich once said on Carson’s show that if marketing...

ctx.x: Do the distributors — I can address this to either of you — are they pretty honest with giving you what you’re owed?

As a rule. I think they’re mostly, well the distributorship and all of those people, they make money by what’s popular and of course what’s popular is rock & roll or heavy metal or something like that. So that give more emphasis, I’m sure, to marketing those products. I think Buddy Rich once said on Carson’s show that if marketing, in general, all over, the advertising marketing people would give jazz musicians only one percent of the monies and promotions as they do to country and rock & roll, we’d be satisfied,…
In your career, was there a time, what span of years would you say jazz was most popular?
